questions.question: Does LoRA require updating the base weights during adapter training?
options: No. The base is frozen; the selected adapter parameters receive updates.
Yes, because initializing factor \(B=0\) blocks all gradients until the base matrix moves.
No, and freezing the base weights guarantees that adapted outputs cannot forget the source task.
questions.explanation: LoRA freezes the base parameters while optimizing the named adapter parameters. Verify parameter ownership and actual before/after deltas. Frozen base storage does not imply unchanged behavior or retained capability.
optionFeedback: LoRA freezes the base parameters while optimizing the named adapter parameters. Verify parameter ownership and actual before/after deltas. Frozen base storage does not imply unchanged behavior or retained capability.
With zero B and nonzero A, the B gradient can be nonzero while A initially receives zero gradient. Inspect both adapter gradients.
Adapters can alter behavior even when the base weights are frozen. Test retention and task quality rather than inferring them from frozen storage.
